newsitem.title: UK: Scots archaeologists dig up rare Roman sculpture.
newsitem.headline: Scots archaeologists dig up rare Roman sculpture.

text.p: Archaeologists on Monday recovered a rare, 1,800-year-old Roman sculpture from the silt of a Scottish river and said the find could be part of a treasure-trove.

The work showing a lioness devouring a man was probably used to mark the grave of a high-ranking official, experts said. It was taken to a National Museum of Scotland laboratory in Edinburgh for careful drying prior to display.
The site of the find was on the banks of the River Almond at Cramond, near Edinburgh, below the remains of a fort which stood on what was the edge of the Roman empire.

"I was very excited...and extremely happy that I was the one that found it -- not for the monetary value but because it was a thing of real beauty," ferry operator Robert Graham, who first spotted the carving, told BBC television.
